inputs.text: This is about more than one conviction. France’s new “psychological subjection” law gives authorities a convenient, elastic label to use against communities they want to bring into line. Father Bernard Domini, the abbot leading the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, is being made an example, while the public is being asked to see it as protection. That’s how control becomes normalized: officials decide which beliefs are dangerous, then use vague language to make dissent look like a threat. Today it’s this community; the precedent could be used against anyone inconvenient.
